title: 34 kW Micro Hydropower Plant Design
summary: A completed rural-electrification design study for Kewai Village, Naran, covering the water-to-wire system and its environmental and economic feasibility.
overview: This Complex Engineering Project studied a 34 kW micro hydropower scheme for rural electrification in Kewai Village, Naran, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. The work connects resource and load assessment with turbine-generator selection, civil arrangements, electrical distribution and implementation planning. It is a design study; the illustrations do not establish a constructed or commissioned plant.
approach: Started with head/flow assessment and village load assessment so the generation concept addressed both the water resource and electricity demand.
Selected a cross-flow turbine and a 35 kW induction generator for a scheme with a 34 kW design capacity. The generator selection and plant design capacity describe different parts of the design.
Developed the water-to-wire chain: intake and conveyance, penstock, powerhouse, turbine-generator set, controls, transformer and distribution network.
Brought technical choices into a feasibility assessment covering costs, implementation planning and environmental/economic considerations.
outcomes: Completed the academic design study for a 34 kW micro hydropower scheme.
Projected approximately 146,000 kWh annual generation and a payback below two years under the study assumptions.
The illustrations describe the proposed system and site arrangement. Construction and commissioning are not established by this design record.

problem: Develop a feasible local-generation design for rural electrification in Kewai Village, Naran, connecting the available water resource with community electricity demand.
context: A completed Complex Engineering Project for Power Generation Systems at Air University. The deliverable is a plant-design and feasibility study.
constraints: Resource assessment, civil layout and electrical distribution must be considered as one system rather than treating generator selection as the whole plant.
Annual generation and payback depend on the study assumptions; they are projections rather than operational records.
lessons: Rural electrification design connects generation equipment with the civil works, controls and distribution needed to serve a community.
Technical capacity, expected energy delivery and economic feasibility are different design questions and need to be reported separately.
